scenes.title: Choose what a shared display should answer

captions.text: Resgrid Big Board brings department information into configurable widgets.
Here, the Personnel table shows operational status beside
staffing, with a clock below it.
A duty supervisor can use this display to review readiness during a handover.
The same approach can support a security control room, search-and-rescue
coordination desk, community paramedicine or mental health response team,
wildland contractor, industrial response team, or fire and E M S department.
This walkthrough builds a readable board using fictional training data.

scenes.title: Start with the actual widget chooser

captions.text: Start on the empty dashboard.
The message directs you to the plus button in the upper right.
Select it to open Add Widget.
The chooser includes Calls, Units, Personnel and Time.
Add those four widgets for this exercise, choosing each from the menu.
The chooser also offers other widget types.
Add information for a specific audience and purpose; a coordination
desk and a shared briefing display may need different amounts of detail.

scenes.title: Give the Calls widget enough room

captions.text: Open the settings gear in the header and select Calls.
Scroll to Widget Size.
In this recorded desktop example, Width is ten grid units and Height is four.
Adjust the width and height sliders to give the incident table enough room,
then use Save to return to the board.
Choose sizes for your actual display.
A wider widget gives long incident names and addresses more horizontal space, while
additional height makes more rows visible.

scenes.title: Bring Priority beside the call identifier

captions.text: In Calls settings, find Column Order and the instruction to use the arrows.
Move Priority upward until the first three columns are I D, Priority and Name.
Use the up arrow on the Priority row, then Save.
This changes where the column appears.
It helps a supervisor read an incident identifier and its priority together.
We will check the table itself next, because the returned display is the
useful confirmation of this setting.
The Calls table now begins with I D, Priority and Name.
The warehouse-alarm exercise shows Urgent, while the community medical standby and
vehicle-rescue exercise show Routine.
Address, Timestamp and Dispatched provide more context across each row.
Read these values together when comparing work.
The Dispatched column lists dispatched recipients; this screen does not by itself
verify that every recipient accepted the assignment or arrived at the incident.
Use the relevant response and operational views for those checks.

scenes.title: Set the Units table order and dimensions

captions.text: Open the gear again and select Units Widget.
In the column-order controls, move State immediately after Name.
Keep Station, Type and Timestamp after those columns for this example.
The Widget Size controls below give this table a width of ten
and a height of three grid units.
Save and inspect the result.
Putting the resource name beside its state makes it easier to scan which vehicle or
team needs attention during a briefing.

scenes.title: Compare resource states and update age

captions.text: On the resulting Units table, Engine fifty-one is Available, Squad
three is Responding, and Reserve Engine fifty-one is Out of Service.
The community-response vehicle demonstrates that the table can include
resources beyond fire apparatus.
A security patrol vehicle or industrial response resource can
be organized using the same fields.
Read Updated as well as State.
Several fictional exercise entries are days old, so a displayed state alone is
not evidence of a fresh readiness report.
Select Personnel in the configuration tabs and find Column Order.
For this example, place Status immediately after Name, followed by Group and
Staffing, then Timestamp and Roles.
Use the arrows on each row to move the columns, then Save.
This arrangement brings an individual and their operational status together
while keeping team assignment, staffing and qualifications
visible elsewhere in the same row.
Choose a sequence that your supervisors can read consistently during handover.
The Personnel table shows Status and Staffing as separate columns.
In this exercise, Darren Ritter has Standing By under Status
and Delayed under Staffing.
Blake Gallo has Standing By and Unavailable.
These are different pieces of information, so read both before
deciding that someone is ready for work.
Roles and Group add organizational context, and Updated provides
the displayed age of the entry.
The Time widget below supplies a visible clock alongside the readiness information.

scenes.title: Enter edit mode and find the widget controls

captions.text: Return to the dashboard and select Edit in the header.
The button changes to Done, and widget headings show a
grip and a red removal control.
A temporary Notes widget has been added beside Time for this layout exercise.
The grip is the place to begin moving the widget.
Check the heading before using a removal control, so you change
the intended panel rather than another widget on a crowded display.
Drag the temporary Notes widget by its heading grip to the right.
The resulting view shows Notes farther across the board, with
Time remaining on the left.
This is a layout change.
It does not change the department note itself.
Use the same placement check when arranging a shared display: confirm
the final location of the panel and make sure important information
is still visible at the distance from which people will read it.

scenes.title: Remove the temporary panel and finish editing

captions.text: Select the red removal control on the temporary Notes widget.
That panel disappears, and the board returns to four widgets:
Calls, Units, Personnel and Time.
The pictured lower part of the board shows Personnel and Time remaining.
Select Done to leave edit mode.
Removing this display widget does not delete the underlying department note.
Keep only the panels needed for this particular display, then check that
its important tables remain readable.

scenes.title: Reload and verify the saved display

captions.text: Reload Big Board to check the saved result.
Calls still begins with I D, Priority and Name.
Scroll down to confirm that Personnel keeps its chosen sequence and
that Time remains on the board.
In this example, the larger tables require scrolling.
For a wall display, choose a smaller set of panels that fits the screen
and verify it on the actual monitor.
For an interactive coordination desk, decide which tables staff will
scroll through during routine work.
